title: WarHub Boxed Set Contents
description: What is inside each boxed set: a product that contains paints, mapped to the paint records it contains. Keyed by product id, so a consumer holding a product does one lookup -- scan a box, resolve the barcode through barcodes.json to a product id, look that id up here, and follow each member's paintId into paints.json for the colour. Only products whose source states their contents appear; a product absent from this document is not a product known to contain nothing. READ contentSkusFrom BEFORE TREATING A MEMBER LIST AS COMPLETE: only one of its three values means the source published an exhaustive list.

counts.description: sets (boxed sets published), refs (every content code that reached this relation), members (refs resolved to a paint id), paints (distinct paints reachable through it), unresolved (refs carrying a reason instead of a paint), unresolvedAtPublish (the subset of those refused by this build rather than upstream -- normally 0; a non-zero value means the paint catalog and the relation were built from different data). members + unresolved == refs always.

sets.description: Keyed by product id, exactly as published in products.json -- manufacturer casing preserved, not camelCased and not normalized.

name.description: A review label copied off the product record, so this document is readable on its own. The product record is authoritative; never join on this.

contentSkusFrom.description: HOW THE SOURCE STATED ITS CONTENTS, and therefore how much the member list is worth. These are three different claims and are kept apart deliberately -- flattening them would misstate the weaker ones. 'stated': the source published a machine-readable contents array, which is exhaustive by construction -- this IS the box. 'description': the codes were read out of the source's own prose, which is editorial and NOT guaranteed exhaustive -- treat the member list as a LOWER BOUND on the box, since a page may state a colour count in words and enumerate only some of them. 'sku': the source published no list at all; the membership is derived from its own code scheme, where a multi-unit case pack's code plus a suffix is the single pot it holds. A 'sku' set therefore has exactly ONE member and is exhaustive in colours while saying nothing about multiplicity -- a Pack of 6 contains six of that one paint, and the pack size lives in `name`, not in `quantity`.

members.description: The paints in this box, in the order the source lists them. Always present; empty when no ref resolved.

unresolved.description: Content codes that could NOT be turned into a paint, published with their reason rather than dropped, so a partially-resolved box is never mistaken for a smaller one. Omitted entirely when every ref resolved.

paintId.description: The paint record in paints.json, brand-slug/paint-slug. This is the link, and it is attached here at publish time because it cannot be derived from the other fields: an id gains a content-derived qualifying suffix when its name collides inside its brand, which is a property of the whole brand file rather than of this row. The paint's brand and product code are deliberately not repeated on this record -- follow the id.

ref.description: The manufacturer's OWN code for this item, verbatim from the source and before any normalization -- the audit link back to the product's content list. It may differ from the resolved paint's productCode: a source that zero-pads prints '09030' for the paint stored as '9030'.

quantity.description: How many of this item the source states the box contains. ABSENT MEANS THE SOURCE DID NOT SAY -- it does not mean one. No source in this catalog states a count today, so this key is currently present on no member.

resolvedBy.description: Present only when the printed ref did NOT identify this paint on its own, naming what settled it instead. Absent -- the overwhelming majority -- means the code resolved directly. 'statedName': the set listed one code twice and the name printed beside the second occurrence identified the paint. 'correction': a human declared, in a reviewed committed file scoped to this one product, that the manufacturer mistyped a code in its own contents list. In both cases `ref` still carries what the source printed, so the repair is visible rather than laundered.

statedName.description: The paint name the source printed beside the ref, carried alongside resolvedBy: statedName as the evidence for that resolution.

ref.description: The content code, verbatim, that names no paint this release publishes.

reason.description: Why it was refused, in prose. HUMAN TEXT, NOT A STABLE VOCABULARY -- the wording is written for whoever will fix the underlying gap and may change without a schema version. A consumer should key on a ref being in this array at all, never on matching this string.
